definitions.explanation: Flowers or leaves dried flat under weight, used for cards, framed art, and craft. Also the craft of making them — a popular hobby for children and a long-standing decorative art.

examples.japanese: {押|お}し{花|ばな}を{作|つく}った。
{本|ほん}の{間|あいだ}に{挟|はさ}んで{押|お}し{花|ばな}にした。
examples.english: I pressed it between the pages of a book to make a pressed flower.

examples.japanese: {祖母|そぼ}は{押|お}し{花|ばな}で{作|つく}ったしおりを{大切|たいせつ}に{保管|ほかん}していた。
examples.english: My grandmother carefully kept the bookmark she had made from pressed flowers.

notes:
{押|お}し (pressing) + {花|はな} (flower); the second element voices to ばな in the compound. A classic summer-vacation craft project for elementary school children.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {押|お}し{花|ばな}を{作|つく}る: to make pressed flowers
- {押|お}し{花|ばな}にする: to turn into a pressed flower
- {押|お}し{花|ばな}のしおり: a pressed-flower bookmark
- {押|お}し{花|ばな}{教室|きょうしつ}: pressed-flower class

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ドライフラワー: dried flowers — air-dried, three-dimensional, not pressed flat
- {標本|ひょうほん}: specimen — a more scientific term, for plants preserved for study
